A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
apolipoproteins A-V, B-48, and E, and the receptor associated protein share common binding sites on members of the low-density lipoprotein receptor superfamily.
apolipoproteins A-I and A-V interact with the low density receptor-related protein (LDLR-RP) and SorLA, two members of the LDL receptor family.
the apolipoprotein is able to bind to members of the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDL-R) gene family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
apolipoproteins A-I and A-V are capable of binding to the LDL receptor-related protein and SorLA, and that this binding is calcium dependent.
apolipoproteins A-I and A-V are both capable of interacting with members of the LDL receptor family.
apolipoproteins are not just inert carriers of lipids, but are also involved in the regulation of lipid metabolism by interacting with cell surface receptors.
